transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-07-08 15:00 UTC; Duration: 48m; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO - Lyon), Elliot Green (ML Eng), Samir Patel (Infra), Rowan (PM)
Links referenced: Lyon infra diagram (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), Redwood dedicated SKU deck (link)

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining uh we'll do quick intros and then dive into your current setup.
[00:10] Priya: hi thanks, i'm priya, cto at lyon, quick note, we run most of our user-facing chat on OpenAI hosted right now, but we also run vLLM locally for some internal tooling and experiment with TGI models.
[00:25] Diego: cool, thanks. when you say OpenAI hosted, are you on the gpt-4 family or a fine-tuned variant?
[00:32] Elliot: gpt-4.1 turbo endpoint, with a small fine-tune for safety/brand voice. We handle about 600 rps at peak between websockets and http calls.
[00:45] Samir: infra note, latency spikes during business hours, cost is escalating and we want more predictability. Also need VPC and KMS integration for some clients.
[01:00] Ava: totally makes sense. high-level, Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, private networking options, and you can pin model versions. Curious — what are your SLOs and hard constraints?
[01:12] Priya: 95th percentile under 150ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), and we want ability to scale for longer contexts to 4k without regression. Also, our security team requires SOC2 + SSO integration, and we'd like audit logs for all inference calls.
[01:30] Diego: we can do that. a couple of things on model parity — you mentioned fine-tunes. do you plan to bring the tuned weights, or keep the behavior via prompt engineering?
[01:40] Elliot: we have the fine-tune artifacts but the weights are with OpenAI's service; we don't have raw-model checkpoints locally. we've tried converting some experiments to vLLM/TGI formats but hit tokenizer mismatches and some soft-failure in safety tuning.
[01:58] Ava: that's common. migration paths: 1) use Redwood Hosted with same model family + eval parity checks; 2) move to Dedicated with a compatible model compiled on the Dedicated runtime; 3) Private for on-prem if you need full control. each has tradeoffs on cost and control.
[02:20] Rowan: quick Q — our legal team is pushy on data residency, some enterprise customers insist data never leaves region. Can Dedicated be region pinned?
[02:28] Diego: yes, you can pin deployments to a region and we support VPC peering and private networking. for Private on-prem we can ship an appliance but that's usually later in the roadmap.
[02:40] Priya: on compatibility — we use vLLM for offline workloads, and TGI for some model serving. what's the story on tokenizer/LLM parity?
[02:50] Diego: our runtime supports most HF-compatible tokenizers and we do a tokenizer normalization pass. where we see drift is with custom fine-tunes from proprietary toolchains. for that we'd run an eval-parity suite comparing outputs on a held-out prompt set — Diego will share the checklist.
[03:10] Elliot: can you run our evals with both openai and the dedicated runtime? we need exact or near-exact output to avoid re-certifying downstream.
[03:18] Ava: yes, we offer eval parity engagements — we can run side-by-side, and if there's a gap we can propose model variants or quantization profiles to reduce drift. sometimes small prompt tweaks are needed.
[03:30] Samir: networking question — do you support VPC peering or only private endpoints? we need control over egress and allowlist.
[03:38] Diego: Dedicated supports VPC peering, private subnets, and customer-controlled NAT egress. also KMS/HSM integrations for key wrapping. we'll provide our networking diagram.
[03:50] Priya: compliance — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation? and how long is audit log retention?
[03:58] Ava: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, can share certs; audit log retention is configurable as an add-on. for Dedicated/Private customers we typically export logs to your SIEM as well.
[04:10] Elliot: perf — any public numbers for 8k context and sequence length? we saw some vendors struggle with kv cache memory blowing up.
[04:18] Diego: our runtime has optimized KV cache management and continuous batching. typical 8k context throughput depends on model and GPU (A100 vs H100) but we can run a baseline test using your prompt set. we'll also test against vLLM/TGI to ensure comparable throughput.
[04:40] Priya: what's the uplift in latency for heavy batching? some of our PL flows need single-digit latencies at low QPS.
[04:47] Diego: batching improves throughput at cost of single-request latency; we can configure autoscaling and small batch sizes with pre-warmed GPUs to hit low-latency SLOs. Dedicated gives predictable capacity which helps.
[05:05] Rowan: cost question — moving to Dedicated, how do we think about committed spend vs on-demand?
[05:12] Ava: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; you get better unit economics. Hosted is usage-based. We can model your current spend — please share sample invoice/usage and we'll produce a cost comparison.
[05:25] Priya: we have a subset of workflows still on vLLM for internal tools; is it realistic to keep vLLM for those and move user-facing to Redwood?
[05:34] Diego: yes, hybrid is common — keep local vLLM for internal workloads and route public traffic to Redwood via smart routing. fallback policies can route to cheaper endpoints on overflow.
[05:45] Elliot: any gotchas when converting TGI model weights? we hit issues around quantization and tied-embedding layers.
[05:52] Diego: those are typical. we have an onboarding flow for model conversion and quantization profiles; sometimes you need a quick retrain or a small calibration pass.
[06:05] Priya: ok timeline — we're targeting a pilot in Q3, production by end of Q3/Q4. stakeholders: infra (Samir), ML (Elliot), legal/compliance, and product (Rowan).
[06:18] Ava: great — next steps i'll send pricing and the dedicated SKU deck, diego will share the eval parity checklist and perf spreadsheet; priya to send 3 representative prompts and a week of telemetry for spikes.
[06:30] Samir: also please include network diagrams and a runbook for failover.
[06:38] Diego: will do, i'll include notes about vLLM/TGI compat tips.
[06:45] Priya: quick question on support SLA — how fast is on-call for P0 incidents?
[06:50] Ava: enterprise SLAs include 1-hour P0; we offer 24/7 support for Dedicated customers as an add-on.
[07:00] Rowan: final, can you try a quick demo of latency numbers now? we have a 2 minute window.
[07:05] Diego: sure — launching a quick synthetic test, but results are approximate. (typing sounds) okay, local synthetic for a 256 token prompt on an H100 var: p50 45ms, p95 132ms under small batch; matches your target.
[07:30] Elliot: that's promising.
[07:36] Ava: thanks everyone — we'll recap via email and attach artifacts.
[07:40] Priya: thanks, appreciate it.
